newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Bank privatisation plan to be submitted in 14 days.
newsitem.headline: Bank privatisation plan to be submitted in 14 days.

text.p: Czech Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik said on Friday he would submit a plan to the government for the further privatisation of the country's four largest banks within 14 days, the Czech agency CTK reported.

It quoted him as telling a meeting of business managers that he would suggest that shares of Investicni a Postovni Banka (IPB) should be the first to be privatised, and foreign investors would be eligible to participate.
"I will recommend that (the privatisation plan) begin with the privatisation of Investicni a Postovni Banka," Kocarnik told the Central European Management Association.
He said his plan would call for the state first to fully and quickly privatise its 33 percent stake in IPB, and then to sell off shares in the other three banks in phases.
The state would hold on to some of its shares in the remaining three of the so-called "Big Four" banks, but eventually these shares would "go fully into privatisation", Kocarnik was quoted as saying,

The four banks are Ceska Sporitelna a.s., Komercni Banka a.s., and IPB -- which all have had some shares privatised through the government's voucher selloffs -- and Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s. which is controlled through a variety of Czech and Slovak state institutions.
He said foreign investors could participate, but no details on how the privatisations might be conducted were given.
"Tested and reknowned foreign banks could be beneficial to our money markets," he said.
He stressed that the plan was based on his opinion and the final decision rested with the cabinet.

Kocarnik last week said that international investment banks such as JP Morgan, Merrill Lynch and Salomon Brothers had been lobbying him during a recent visit to Washington, pushing for the further privatisation of the Big Four.
Analysts have said further privatisation of the Big Four, which control over 70 percent of Czech banking activity, would bring more efficiency and competition to the banking sector.
The Czech state through its National Property Fund still controls a 45.09 percent stake in Sporitelna, and a 48.74 percent stake in Komercni Banka.
